newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shekel up sharply on dollar in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Israel shekel up sharply on dollar in early trade.

text.p: The Israeli shekel was up strongly for the second day running in early afternoon trading on Wednesday, but the atmosphere remains uncertain, dealers said.
The dollar was trading at 3.5064 shekels at about 1000 GMT, down 1.2 percent from Tuesday's representative rate of 3.5490. Since the dollar peaked last Friday, it has lost about 2.4 percent.
Against the basket of foreign currencies, which comprises the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, the shekel was trading at 3.8023, versus 3.894 on Tuesday.
"The market has got its confidence back in the shekel," said Shiko Angert, a dealer at Union Bank. "Speculators who sold the dollar two weeks ago realised they don't have to rush back to buy it."
The shekel tumbled five percent in the last week of June after the government instituted changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates 1.2 percentage points.
"We have't seen massive selling but there are no bids," Angert said. "Probably 3.49-3.50 is the psychological level to show some bidding."

Dealers said spreads had narrowed this morning to 30 to 50 points but widened again later in the day to 70-100. "The spreads are still very wide. The market is still nervous," said Ilan Viskin of Bank Hapoalim.

He said the market was too jittery to make any short-term predictions of where the currency would settle, but Angert said he expected the shekel would reach the bottom end of its trading band against the currency basket next week. That, he added, would touch off Bank of Israel intervention.
The basket rate was 2.07 percent above the band in early afternoon.
